pigeon noun

also dove, pigeons, pigeon coop, dovecote, wood pigeon, coo

classical

Traupman 144
Cic.

columba, columbae f.

noun, first declension

pigeon, dove

Other words

  • columbārium, columbāriī n. — a dovecote, pigeon house

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Varr. RR 3.7.4 (Lewis & Short); Col. 8.8.3; Traupman 144

  • palumbēs, palumbis m./f. — wood pigeon, ring-dove

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 142; Traupman 306

    Lewis & Short: also palumbis, palumbus, palumba.

  • gemō, gemere, gemuī, gemitum — to coo (of doves)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. E. 1.59: turtur ab ulmō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 142, 144; Traupman 296

    Properly “sigh, groan”, said of the mournful cry of animals; of the turtle-dove in Vergil.

Examples

  • avēs magnae inter columbās gravī gradū ambulābant

    big birds were walking with heavy steps among the pigeonsLibellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

  • Columbae gemunt.

    Pigeons coo.Traupman 360
